title: Read compiler diagnostics
goal: Find the first diagnostic, fix it, and check the meaning of the result separately.

prerequisites.text: Run a C17 program in Code Studio.
Read a variable declaration and a printf call.

terms.title: Diagnostic
terms.definition: A compiler message describing a problem. It often gives a file, location, and reason.

terms.title: Identifier
terms.definition: A name used in a program, such as cargo. Letter order and case matter.

terms.title: Standard output
terms.definition: Text printed by a running program. Read build diagnostics separately.

sections.title: How to find the cause
paragraphs: You open an example and rename a variable, but change its name in only one place. Clicking Run compiles the code first. An error may appear before the program starts.
Find the first error message in your own source. Read the file name, line, column, and description. Later messages may follow from the first one.
After correcting the error, rebuild and check the output. A program that builds can still calculate something different from what the task requires.

sections.title: A working line and a typo
paragraphs: In the working version, cargo is declared and its name matches in the call to printf. In a copy, change only the printf argument to carog.
steps: Run the original example. The declaration and the reference in printf use the same name. The program prints Cargo: 7.
In a copy, change only cargo → carog in printf. Look for a Clang message containing undeclared identifier and the name carog. The column number depends on your formatting.
Change carog back to cargo. After rebuilding, check the single line of stdout again.

sections.title: Two short experiments
paragraphs: Remove the semicolon after int cargo = 7. Clang reports expected and points near the place where the semicolon belongs. Check the reported line and the end of the line before it.
Change 7 to 6 and compilation still succeeds. The program prints Cargo: 6. Compare that with the intended Cargo: 7 by running it.

sections.title: A successful build and a correct result
paragraphs: Start by changing the smallest fragment that explains the first message. When the build succeeds again, check the calculation on known data.
Record the build outcome and the stdout of a later run separately. This lets you verify the name fix and the formula fix.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Check the diagnostic requirement, scope of names, and expression statements.

selfcheck.prompt: What happens after changing cargo to carog only in printf?
feedback: The expression refers to an undeclared name.
Compilation fails before the program starts.
The compiler cannot launch the program with this error.

selfcheck.prompt: The build succeeds but the program prints Total: 13 instead of Total: 19. What should you inspect first?
options: The location of a compile error
feedback: 16 - 3 = 13, but the task asks you to add 3.
This successful build contains no such error.
The output shows that the program ran.

selfcheck.prompt: What two distinct facts should you record after fixing the spelling and formula?
selfcheck.feedback: The build succeeds. A subsequent run produces the expected stdout.

practice.title: Diagnose two problems in a calculation
practice.task: A shipment holds 16 base items and 3 additional items. First fix the build error in the starter. Then make it print Total: 19 by computing the result from base and extra.
criteria: Name the undeclared identifier bas and correct the reference.
After fixing the name, observe Total: 13 separately.
The final total is computed from base and extra and the program prints Total: 19.
practice.hint: The first run exposes a name problem. Once the build succeeds, compare the operator with the word additional.

steps.action: Run the starter, read the first diagnostic, and fix the name only.
steps.why: Change one cause at a time.

steps.action: Run again and compare the output with the task.
steps.expected: The program prints Total: 13, but the expected total is 19.

steps.action: Fix the expression and run once more.
steps.why: The calculation must be checked in stdout.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: In a copy of the correct version, set extra to 0, predict the output, and test. Why could the wrong operator go unnoticed with zero?
criteria: Adding and subtracting zero have the same result.
The case extra = 3 distinguishes the formulas.

teaching.scene: After a rename, the cargo report stops producing fresh output. Find the difference between the declared name and the name used in the call, then verify the value in a successful run.

predict.prompt: The declared cargo value is 7. Which identifier does the working example pass to printf, and which output confirms the match?
predict.answer: printf uses cargo, exactly as declared. The build succeeds, %d receives 7 and stdout shows Cargo: 7.

apply.prompt: A new version declares `int seats = 3;` and passes `seat` to printf. How do you distinguish the outcomes before and after correcting the name?
apply.answer: Clang reports that seat is undeclared, so the original build yields no fresh output. After changing the name to seats, a successful run can print 3.

practice.strategy: Start with the first diagnostic and compare its identifier with the declaration. Build after that one edit. Once execution works, verify the formula with the two input values.
practice.diagnosis: When the bas diagnostic disappears and Total is still wrong, the name fix worked. Investigate the expression supplying the value to printf.

syntax.explanation: A declaration binds an identifier to a variable. In a printf argument, the compiler resolves the name within its scope.
syntax.mistake: seat and seats are distinct identifiers. Match the exact spelling in the diagnostic and declaration.
